headline: Heavier rain and breezy winds arrive overnight and Sunday, showers linger Monday, and unsettled seasonal weather continues through the week.
summary: As of Saturday evening, a storm system off the coast is moving in and will slowly drift south and east through Monday morning. Light rain is already reaching the north Olympic Peninsula. A cold front (the leading edge of cooler air) should move onshore overnight and bring heavier rain than Saturday's light rain. Forecasters call it a fairly typical October storm, but the first fall-like one of the season. Through Sunday evening they expect about 1 to 2 inches of rain along the coast and Olympic Peninsula, and about 0.50 to 1 inch along the I-5 corridor and eastward. South winds pick up on the coast this evening, spread inland with the front, and stay breezy through Sunday, with gusts of 20 to 35 mph possible in many areas. Scattered but widespread showers should linger well into Monday and move east late Monday afternoon. Highs should be near normal, in the mid to upper 50s, and overnight lows cooler than normal, from the low 30s to the low 40s. A weaker disturbance Tuesday should mostly bring light rain south of western Washington. A stronger system arrives Tuesday night into Wednesday, much like this weekend's storm, with cooler temperatures and widespread rain. Showery, unsettled weather is expected Thursday through Saturday. Forecasters are fairly confident in the overall pattern, but less sure about the exact path of the surface low on Monday: one model group brings it into Grays Harbor late Monday morning, while others keep it much farther south. The strength and timing of Tuesday's disturbance also vary between model runs. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for land areas. Gale Warnings and Small Craft Advisories are in effect for the coastal waters and the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with seas building to 8 to 12 feet tonight.
changes: Early Saturday, forecasters expected only light rain from a weak system; by the afternoon they described a wetter, breezier storm with a cold front overnight, 1 to 2 inches of coastal rain, and showers lingering into Monday. Gale Warnings were added for some coastal waters, and the Wednesday system was described as a stronger, widespread rain event.
